name: Laxmi Narasimha Reddy Gumreddy
title: Qualtrics · Sr. Systems Engineer | DevSecOps Security
description: I’m a Sr. Systems Engineer at Qualtrics (DevSecOps Security) with 8+ years of experience turning complex infrastructure into reliable, secure platforms. I care most about the moments that matter in production: keeping customer-facing systems within SLA, making incidents easier to diagnose, and closing the gap between “we deployed it” and “we can trust it in prod.”

Today at Qualtrics, I operate multi-region AWS EKS and Nomad estates—network policy with Cilium, policy enforcement with OPA/Kyverno, GitOps with ArgoCD, and observability with Prometheus, Grafana, and the Elastic Stack. I’ve also driven container supply-chain security: signed images, pipeline scanning, and admission controls so only vetted artifacts reach production.

Outside the day-to-day runbooks, I build tools that reflect how I actually work on call—and increasingly how I work with agents. That’s how klew.dev came to life: a local macOS app for Kubernetes incidents, with MCP so coding agents can help investigate using the same cluster context you see in the UI.

featuredBuild.label: What I've built
featuredBuild.name: klew.dev
featuredBuild.tagline: Kubernetes incident investigation—for you and your agents
featuredBuild.story: During outages, context is scattered: workloads in one pane, events in another, logs in a third. klew.dev pulls workloads, events, logs, and resource state into a single macOS desktop app so you can follow a failure line-by-line without juggling tabs or sending cluster data to a SaaS backend. It also exposes an MCP server so coding agents can query cluster context and help investigate incidents alongside you—still local-first, with no cluster data shipped to a third-party SaaS.
highlights: Local-first: connects via kubeconfig and the Kubernetes API (client-go); your data stays on your machine.
MCP integration lets AI agents access investigation tools and cluster context safely on your machine, not through a remote black box.
Live watches plus periodic snapshots, with Drain3 clustering so repeated log and event patterns surface as one story.
Built for on-call engineers (and the agents they pair with) when minutes matter.
